chunks: And through his chain of narration, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! Do not follow the first glance with a second glance, for you are only excused for the first glance.'

key_terms.النَّظَرَةَ: The act of looking or gazing
key_terms.يُتْبِعِ: To follow or succeed (in this context, to follow a look with another)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on following an initial glance with a second look in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, establishes the principle of 'al-nazara al-ula' (the first glance) as a natural, excusable reflex, while 'ittiba' al-nazara' (following it with a deliberate second look) constitutes the sin. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is foundational for understanding the gradual process of visual temptation, emphasizing that moral accountability begins with the conscious decision to linger or focus after the initial accidental sight.
